channel.title: AI News Digest
channel.description: Official AI product updates from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and GitHub

item.title: OpenAI and ServiceNow expand partnership across enterprise workflows
item.description: OpenAI and ServiceNow expand their partnership to bring OpenAI models and agents into ServiceNow and ServiceNow workflows into ChatGPT and Codex.

item.title: Legora is building the agentic operating system for legal work
item.description: See how Legora uses OpenAI models, ChatGPT, and Codex to accelerate legal workflows, expand contract analysis, and free lawyers to focus on higher-value work.

item.title: API credits for ChatGPT subscribers
item.description: Eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers can now claim up to $500 per month in free API credits as a subscription benefit. Activate the benefit from ChatGPT or API Platform by linking an API organization you own.

item.title: Use a single regional Agent Registry instance for Gemini Enterprise apps
item.description: Change Use a single regional Agent Registry instance for Gemini Enterprise apps For Gemini Enterprise apps, we recommend associating each Agent Gateway with a single regional Agent Registry instance in the same project and region as the gateway. Use the us-central1 registry for global and us apps, and the europe-west1 registry for eu apps. This note updates the September 9, 2026 entry. For more information, see Register your agents and destination resources.

item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: Our next frontier model
item.description: Gemini 4 Carbon: Our next frontier model

item.title: Work from anywhere with a new, connected Copilot cloud experience
item.description: Copilot is now one connected experience in the cloud. Start a cloud task wherever you are, on github.com, GitHub Mobile, the Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, VS Code, or right from a conversation in Slack or Microsoft Teams.

item.title: Security extension for the GitHub Copilot app
item.description: You can now work through your repository’s GitHub code scanning alerts without leaving the GitHub Copilot app. The new GitHub security extension, now in public preview, lets you find the alerts that matter most and ask Copilot to explain or help fix them.

item.title: Route and orchestrate models with GitHub Copilot Fusion
item.description: GitHub Copilot Fusion is generally available. Instead of picking a model for each task, choose Copilot Fusion and let Copilot intelligently route and orchestrate which models it uses for you.

item.title: Push protection beyond predefined secret patterns
item.description: GitHub push protection is expanding beyond secrets with predefined formats. Developed in collaboration with Microsoft Applied Sciences, our new purpose-built classifier evaluates how potential secrets are used in surrounding code, allowing GitHub to block secrets even without a known and recognizable format.

item.title: Prioritize Dependabot alerts with reachability analysis
item.description: Dependabot alerts can add up faster than a team can work through them. A vulnerable package in your dependency tree doesn’t always mean your code uses the vulnerable part of it, so knowing whether it does gives you more context when deciding where to start.

item.title: Issue artifacts are now in public preview
item.description: Issue artifacts attach agent-generated outputs and other important context directly to an issue. By keeping plans, research, links, and visualizations alongside the work, they give coding agents richer context and teams a durable record as the work evolves.

item.title: Introducing Replica, an open-source AI prototyping tool
item.description: We’re open sourcing Replica, an AI-powered prototyping tool created by GitHub Design that helps anyone on your product team turn ideas into interactive prototypes using your own design system. Music: “Electrodoodle” by Kevin MacLeod ( incompetech.com ), licensed under CC BY 4.0.

item.title: GitHub intelligence puts your code, context, and history to work
item.description: Agents should understand more than your codebase—they should understand how your team works. Your preferences, repository conventions, skills, and custom instructions guide how changes should be made, while code in related repositories can show how the pieces fit together.

item.title: GitHub Enterprise now includes access to GitHub Copilot
item.description: Enterprises working with a GitHub or Microsoft account team can now get Copilot included with GitHub Enterprise for every licensed user. Previously, you had to manage two things: how many Copilot seats you were paying for and how much AI usage those users consumed.

item.title: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Universe releases
item.description: This year, we focused on giving you more choice in how you work with GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code: which models you use, where your agents run, and how you stay involved. Keep work moving without staying at your desk or in one tool.

item.title: GitHub Copilot in JetBrains Universe releases
item.description: Today, we’re making GitHub Copilot in JetBrains more capable, secure, and seamless. From GitHub Copilot Fusion’s smarter model orchestration to local sandboxes and next edit suggestions (NES), this update brings powerful improvements to how you build, review, and manage work.

item.title: GitHub Copilot Fusion now supports selection of local models
item.description: Today we are shipping intelligent routing for local models into experimental preview. GitHub Copilot Fusion can now choose between supported on-device models and cloud models, enabling intelligent local model routing in GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot app, and Visual Studio Code.

item.title: GitHub Copilot app, Universe releases
item.description: Work doesn’t always fit in a single repository or session. A feature can span several repositories.

item.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows generally available
item.description: GitHub Agentic Workflows, an open source project from GitHub Next, is now generally available. With agentic workflows, you can automate reasoning-based tasks like issue triage, CI failure analysis, documentation updates, and test writing by using coding agents inside GitHub Actions.

item.title: Generate and edit images directly in Copilot
item.description: You can now generate and edit images using natural language in GitHub Copilot. When you ask for an image, your selected reasoning model calls a dedicated image-generation tool powered by GPT Image 2.5 Flare, previews the result inline, and saves it to your project.

item.title: Code scanning for AI applications in public preview
item.description: Code scanning can now detect AI applications and agent vulnerabilities, including indirect prompt injection (XPIA), sensitive information disclosure, excessive agency, and other AI-specific risks as coverage expands. Scans automatically run on pull requests.

item.title: Build shared workflows for your team with Copilot Automations
item.description: Shared Copilot Automations are rolling out, enabling teams to build and maintain AI-powered workflows together. With Copilot Automations, you can combine prompts, triggers, and tools to design workflows around the way your team works.

item.title: AI Scan for repositories in public preview
item.description: You can now use AI Scan to find vulnerabilities across your whole repository, not just in pull request changes. It covers languages and frameworks that CodeQL doesn’t support and finds issues that rule-based analysis can miss in languages CodeQL already covers.

item.title: Introducing Agent Skills
item.description: Claude can now use Skills to improve how it performs specific tasks. Skills are folders that include instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude can load when needed. Claude will only access a skill when it's relevant to the task at hand.

item.title: Fine-tune Claude 3 Haiku in Amazon Bedrock
item.description: Claude 3 Haiku can now be fine-tuned in Amazon Bedrock with custom training data, enabling faster, more accurate performance at lower cost. Update: Fine-tuning Claude 3 Haiku in Amazon Bedrock is generally available.

item.title: Announcements
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: AI for Science expands to foundations and institutions
item.description: We’re highlighting 20 scientific foundations, institutions, and research groups from around the world that we’ve partnered with in an expansion of our AI for Science program.

item.title: Retell uses OpenAI models to help power 100M monthly calls
item.description: GPT-6 Astra tops Retell’s voice agent benchmark, while Codex helps it reach a $1.6M annual revenue run rate per employee.

item.title: OpenAI expands partnership with Oracle to bring its apps to ChatGPT
item.description: OpenAI and Oracle are expanding their partnership to bring business applications and AI agents into ChatGPT and power new Oracle offerings.

item.title: How Check Point accelerates vulnerability research with Daybreak
item.description: With OpenAI Daybreak, Check Point speeds up the research behind new security protections, enabling its analysts to turn vulnerability intelligence into customer defenses faster.

item.title: Gemini Robotics ER 2 (Preview)
item.description: Feature Gemini Robotics ER 2 (Preview) Gemini Robotics ER 2 ( gemini-robotics-er-2-preview ) is available in Preview. Gemini Robotics ER 2 is an embodied reasoning vision-language model built on Gemini 3.5 Flash for robotics applications, including spatial reasoning, agentic code execution, task orchestration, and video understanding. Feature xAI's Grok 4.7 is generally available Grok 4.7 is now generally available (GA) for production use on the global endpoint and the US multi-region endpoint.

item.title: Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation
item.description: Genie 4: our new world model unlocking unprecedented realism in real-time simulation.

item.title: GitHub Copilot supports server-to-server authentication
item.description: GitHub Copilot now supports server-to-server authentication for GitHub Apps installed on organizations, available in public preview. Services and agents built with the GitHub Copilot SDK can now make requests on behalf of an organization without relying on a signed-in user’s credentials.

item.title: Partnerships
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra
item.description: Bringing fast and capable computer use to everyone

item.title: GPT-6.1 Sol helps CodeRabbit strengthen security across complex codebases
item.description: CodeRabbit uses GPT-6.1 Sol to investigate security risks across complex codebases. Its security agent helps developers review findings and proposed fixes.

item.title: How Fanatics and OpenAI streamline the fan experience
item.description: Fanatics uses OpenAI to help fans complete their game-day outfits with Shop the Look. Testing across roughly 30,000 MLB products showed 10% higher engagement.

item.title: ChatGPT’s expanding world of work
item.description: Explore OpenAI Signals data on 165 work activities across nearly 100 countries, revealing how people use ChatGPT for work and how usage changes over time.

item.title: Working with academic communities to build scientific understanding
item.description: OpenAI shares model results on the Kakeya conjecture, Exponential Time Hypothesis, and quantum chromodynamics—and how researchers can verify and build on them.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Terra in GitHub Copilot
item.description: GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI’s newest model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for everyday agentic coding and terminal work at a lower cost than GPT-6.1 Sol.

item.title: GitHub Copilot assisted permissions generally available
item.description: Assisted permissions are now generally available in GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot app, and Visual Studio Code. When Copilot requests permission to run a command, access a file system path, or open a URL, a large language model evaluates the request.

item.title: Anthropic files S-1 with the SEC for proposed initial public offering
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: Securing our frontier model training environment
item.description: OpenAI explains how we strengthened containment for frontier model training and evaluation, including offline environments and high-compute red-teaming.

item.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users (Part II)
item.description: Learn how OpenAI scaled Habitat with reliable multi-tenancy, global caching, and Azure Cosmos DB to deliver 12× faster reads for ChatGPT.

item.title: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK partner to advance AI safety and security
item.description: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK are partnering on AI safety, security, and technical research to strengthen safeguards and support a more resilient digital ecosystem.

item.title: Usage metrics API adds usage from tools like OpenCode
item.description: The Copilot usage metrics API now reports model usage from more of the tools your developers use with Copilot, including tools like OpenCode that weren’t previously captured in your reports. A new totals_by_client array is available in the enterprise, organization, enterprise-user, and organization-user 1-day and 28-day reports.

item.title: Turn notifications into code with GitHub Copilot in Teams
item.description: The new GitHub app in Teams brings notifications and Copilot together, helping teams turn issues into fixes and ship code faster without leaving the conversation. Get notified in channels, group chats, or private chats, then @mention GitHub to turn updates into action.

item.title: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — September update
item.description: September 2026 brought deeper visibility into your work: explore pull requests without leaving chat, bring the AI model your team trusts, and fix vulnerable packages the moment Visual Studio flags them. Highlights Here’s what’s new with GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio 2026.

item.title: experimental-claude-tag-2026-10-21
item.description: The Claude Tag API is available in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations with the experimental-claude-tag-2026-10-21 beta header. Its /v1/organizations/claude_tag/ endpoints read and change Claude Tag settings on Slack channels and Slack workspaces, show which settings apply in a channel and where each comes from, and attach Access bundles. Call it with an Admin API key that your primary owner creates in claude.ai with the read:claude_tag or write:claude_tag scope.
